title: Wait From Signing to Start of Work — Ridgeline Installation Services
content:
The time a Ridgeline Installation Services customer waited between signing and the start of work sets the wait share of the progress share due at the start of work.

**Clause.** Wait share of the start-of-work payment: the wait is the calendar days from the contract signing date to the date of the installation visit at which work started; a wait of more than the long-wait days of 60 takes the long-wait share of 0.95, a wait of at most the short-wait days of 30 takes the short-wait multiple of 1.05, and any other wait takes a wait share of 1.

The progress share, the program's progress payment percentage of the contract price billed, is multiplied by the wait share before it is rounded to the cent; the share itself is never rounded.

## Terms used

- **The contract signing date** is the date the agreement was signed, from the contract record.
- **The installation visit at which work started** is the most recent installation visit recorded on the contract with the outcome completed as scheduled.

| Wait | Wait share |
|---|---|
| 0 to 30 days | 1.05 |
| 31 to 60 days | 1 |
| 61 days or more | 0.95 |

## Boundary dates (hypothetical agreement signed 1 February of a non-leap year)

| Work started | Wait | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 3 March | 30 | 1.05 |
| 4 March | 31 | 1 |
| 2 April | 60 | 1 |
| 3 April | 61 | 0.95 |

**Hypothetical:** with a progress share of 3000.00 before the wait share, a 25-day wait gives 3150.00 and a 75-day wait gives 2850.00.
